title: KV cache warmup allocation tracing and memory reproducibility harness
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Summary: We observe a slow, persistent GPU RSS growth in long-running continuous-batching workloads when KV cache warmup is enabled. Growth is small per minute but accumulates over days and correlates to increased cudaMallocAsync activity and host staging churn. This ticket scopes building a lightweight allocation-tracing capability, a deterministic memory-replay harness that reproduces the pattern, telemetry additions, and short-term mitigations to reduce fragmentation and staging churn while we root-cause the allocator behaviour.

Background: Several customer and internal services running steady-state traffic with automatic KV warmup enabled show an RSS drift (10-30MB/day) that eventually triggers OOM on capacity-constrained Dedicated nodes. Existing heap snapshots point to many short-lived small allocations (sub-1KB to 8KB) interleaved with occasional large transient buffers. The allocation distribution appears to cause arena splitting and prevents effective coalescing from cudaMallocAsync, producing fragmentation across device pools and frequent pinned-host staging allocations.

Goals: (1) Implement an allocator trace (configurable at runtime) that records: allocation size, cuda stream id, pool id/tag, allocation kind (device/pinned/staging), stack trace or callsite hash, timestamp, and freeing event. Trace must be low overhead (sampling or circular buffer) and selectable via env var. (2) Create a MemReplay harness that can replay a recorded allocation/free trace deterministically against a debug build to reproduce RSS drift and fragmentation. (3) Add telemetry counters and dashboards (allocation lifetime histograms, deferred_free_queue_length, staging_reuse_rate) to surface signals. (4) Ship a short-term mitigation toggle: staging reuse window + coalescing deferred free aggregator to reduce churn.

Risks: tracing overhead could perturb allocation timing—use sampling/circular buffer and enable only in canary. MemReplay must support both CUDA and CPU-local modes. Any allocator change must be validated under peak throughput to avoid regressions in latency.

Deliverables: allocator-trace prototype and docs, MemReplay harness in runtime/tools, dashboard panels, mitigation config flag, test plan and canary rollout steps.
steps_to_repro: 1) Provision a dedicated-small instance (2x A10s) with continuous-batching KV warmup enabled and default staging behavior.
2) Run a synthetic workload that mimics production: 250-600 RPS sustained; 50% requests trigger KV warmup path; sequence lengths 512-2048; run for 24+ hours.
3) Observe device RSS with nvidia-smi or metrics exporter; look for steady climb of ~10-40 MB/day and increased cudaMallocAsync alloc/free churn in allocator metrics.
4) Snapshot /proc/pid/smaps, runtime allocator counters, and kernel traces at 6-hour intervals.
investigation_notes: 2026-02-21 - initial triage: allocator metrics show bursts of small device allocations on a single stream id (~42) coinciding with KV warmup batches. Host staging pages increase in allocation frequency rather than size.
2026-02-25 - ran targeted reproducer with high rate of small prefix loads; reproduced slow RSS drift when warmup concurrency > 4. Disabling warmup removes drift.

2026-02-28 - profiling with cudaMallocAsync debug build: observed repeated allocation/free patterns that leave fragmented free lists in the pool allocator; coalescing not triggered due to allocator internal fragmentation thresholding.

2026-03-03 - confirmed that small repeated pinned-host staging allocations are not being reused across warmup requests due to stream-affined staging buckets being exhausted and never returned quickly enough to global reuse list.

2026-03-07 - hypothesis: combination of small allocation size distribution + stream-local staging + deferred-free ordering is preventing cudaMallocAsync from returning memory to device pools, gradually increasing RSS.
proposed_solution: A) Tracing: Add a lightweight allocation tracer to runtime allocator that emits circular-buffered events (alloc/free) with size, stream id, pool id, allocation_kind, and callsite hash. Expose via RUNTIME_ALLOC_TRACE env var and /debug/alloc_trace endpoint to dump buffer.

B) MemReplay: Implement a deterministic replay tool that can inject recorded allocation/free events into a debug allocator with configurable timing to reproduce fragmentation patterns. Provide mode to run in CPU-only to debug allocation order without CUDA.

C) Short-term mitigation: Add a staging reuse window (configurable ms) and a deferred-free aggregator that batches frees from the same stream into a single return to the pool every X ms. Add env flag RUNTIME_STAGING_REUSE_WINDOW and RUNTIME_FREE_AGGREGATION_MS.
D) Medium-term: Introduce stream-aligned freelists with cross-stream reclamation policy and lower the fragmentation threshold for small-size-class coalescing when warmup traffic is high.

E) Telemetry: Add histograms for allocation lifetimes by size-class, counter for deferred_free_queue_length, and percentage reuse of staging pages. Create Grafana panels and alert rule for abnormal staging_reuse_rate drop.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Tracer: Can be enabled in canary with <5% CPU overhead on representative workload and produces useful event logs that allow identifying the callsites of repeated small allocations.
2) MemReplay: Reproduces the RSS drift locally within 6 hours in deterministic mode with the recorded trace from production-like run.
3) Mitigation: With staging reuse window enabled on canary, RSS growth over 48 hours reduces by >=70% compared to baseline reproducer run.
4) Telemetry: New metrics visible in console and an alert fires when staging_reuse_rate < 60% for 30 minutes.
5) Code review + perf regression tests included; rollout plan documented and QA runbook added.
